clue.text: Fine food, a weakness

blocks.note: first meaning: a choice, rare dish prized by gourmets
second meaning: frailty or fragility of health or build

explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes it read as if a gourmet admits a soft spot for fine food; in fact the two phrases are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a choice dish, and also frailty, as in the delicacy of a sickly child's constitution.

clue.text: A little shade's ignored in sketch

indicators.note: a little of something is only a small portion, so just a short run of letters is wanted

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: An artist leaves out the shading in a quick drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the gap: shaDE'S IGNored, with the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a preliminary drawing or plan, which is one sense of the noun used by artists and architects.

clue.text: Change course: slippery fish turns around with room to manoeuvre

indicators.note: turning around faces the other way, so the letters built so far are read backwards

blocks.note: to yaw is for a ship or plane to swing off its heading
the eel is the proverbially slippery fish

explanation.surface: A sailor steers around a slippery fish in the water, making space to move.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers both pieces together, not just the fish: YAW plus EEL, read backwards, gives LEE + WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is slack or margin for freedom of action, originally the drift a ship makes downwind.

clue.text: Country with value on continent (not France)

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first
saying a word is not there means its letter must be taken away

blocks.note: the cost of something is its value or price
a continent
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: A country is judged by its value to a continent, France excepted.
explanation.walkthrough: F is the international vehicle code for France, so taking it out of the continent's name leaves the second half of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a Central American republic between Nicaragua and Panama, so it is a nation.

clue.text: He’s fed her bacon, fried, for meaty supper

indicators.note: frying cooks and breaks food down, so these letters are scrambled into new order

blocks.note: all fourteen letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A man cooks his partner a fry-up of bacon for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fried' sits comfortably with bacon, which hides that it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Corned beef hash is a dish of chopped salt beef fried with potato, a hearty evening meal.

clue.text: Primarily unrealistic? Thomas once pictured it acerbically!

definitions.text: Primarily unrealistic? Thomas once pictured it acerbically!

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so the opening letter of each following word is wanted

blocks.clueFragment: unrealistic? Thomas once pictured it acerbically
blocks.note: the initial letters of these six words

explanation.surface: A sly remark that Thomas More's imagined world was a sardonic, unrealistic dream.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Sir Thomas More wrote Utopia in 1516, a satirical picture of an ideal but impossible commonwealth.
explanation.definitionFit: More's book named an imaginary perfect society, and the word now means any impractical ideal state.

clue.text: Shin up, Everyman? In a bit

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it, so a letter goes inside the phrase
in a down entry going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
the setter, Everyman, refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the setter will shin up something in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shin up' reads as climbing, but the shin is the definition and 'up' the reversal. I goes into A BIT to make AIBIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the inner, larger bone of the lower leg, commonly called the shinbone.

clue.text: GNP's fine! Rolling in cash ... once

definitions.note: plural coins rather than mass noun cash

indicators.note: rolling things tumble over and over, so the letters are tossed into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: An economist cheers the national output: the country was once rolling in money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling in cash' is a ready-made idiom for wealth, which disguises 'Rolling' as the signal and 'cash ... once' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pfennigs were the small German coins, a hundredth of a mark, withdrawn when the euro arrived.

clue.text: A holy book ... solemn vow ... what else? Finally, something to combat evil

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so the closing letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
NT is the New Testament
the marriage vow 'I do'
the final letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A list of religious defences against evil: scripture, a sacred vow, and anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' seems to introduce the definition, but it acts on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote is a remedy that counteracts poison, and loosely anything that cures or counters an ill.

clue.text: Terribly bad manners, drinking gallons: a Sirah's drained with meal

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so a letter is absorbed into the group
something done terribly is done badly and out of order, so the letters are jumbled
a drained vessel has its contents emptied, leaving only the outside letters

blocks.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for gallons
taken as written
the first and last letters; Sirah is a red wine grape

explanation.surface: A boorish diner guzzles gallons of red wine and drains the glass over dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: G goes into BAD MANNERS, those letters are rearranged, then A and SH follow. Bangers are sausages, and mash is mashed potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangers and mash, sausages with mashed potato, is a classic British pub dish, so it is a meal.

clue.text: Poet writes; 'special' Queen Elizabeth described!

indicators.note: to describe a figure in geometry is to draw a line around it, so outer letters enclose the rest

blocks.note: S is a dictionary abbreviation for special
to pen is to write
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher

explanation.surface: A poet writes about a special subject, Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: Edmund Spenser's The Faerie Queene celebrated Elizabeth I as Gloriana.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan author of The Faerie Queene, a major English verse writer.

clue.text: Marmite regularly seen around in France: well, that's relaxing

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is taken
being seen around something means surrounding it, so those letters wrap the next piece

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
bien is French for well

explanation.surface: Marmite turns up all over France, which is apparently soothing news. Marmite is a yeast-extract spread.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the even letters, not the odd ones, of Marmite; 'in France' tells you to put the next word into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient describes calm, atmospheric music or surroundings meant to soothe, so it can mean restful.

clue.text: Reported harvest in country

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: to garner is to gather in a crop; with a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound alike

explanation.surface: News of a harvest in some country.
explanation.walkthrough: The match relies on British pronunciation, where the R of garner is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana is a West African nation, formerly the Gold Coast, so it fits a state.

clue.text: Instilled deeply in English: bad weather and, regularly, feuds

indicators.note: at regular intervals means alternate letters are taken

blocks.note: Eng is the standard abbreviation
rain is bad weather
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Rain and quarrels are deeply rooted in English life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In English' looks like part of the definition, but 'in' only links and English supplies ENG.
explanation.definitionFit: Something engrained is fixed firmly, like dirt worked into the fibres, so a habit firmly implanted.

clue.text: Whirl twig around welcoming back rub for pilot

indicators.note: sent around means turned about and mixed, so these letters are reordered
back means going in the opposite direction, so the word is read from its end
welcoming someone takes them in, so one group of letters receives another

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone spins a stick about, then gives the pilot a back rub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back rub' is a familiar phrase, but 'back' acts on rub alone. WHIRL and TWIG together are the letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilbur Wright and his brother Orville made the first powered aeroplane flights in 1903, so he was an aviator.

clue.text: Skipping starter, greybeard's chewed baked goods

indicators.note: skipping the starter means passing over the first course, so the opening letter is dropped
chewing mashes things up, so the letters are mixed into new order

blocks.note: the word with its S, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: An old man passes on the first course and munches bread instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' sounds like a dinner course, but it means the first letter, G.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye breads are loaves made with rye flour, products of a baker's oven.

clue.text: In ancient culture, centaurs made merry

indicators.note: making merry is wild revelry, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: In some old civilisation, the half-horse centaurs held a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Centaurs suit a classical scene, which hides that they are only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Etruscan civilisation flourished in central Italy before Rome, so the word names that early people and way of life.

clue.text: Instrument, Japanese (Eastern), sounding out of tune around West

indicators.note: around can mean near or close by, so the pieces simply sit side by side

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for Japanese
E for Eastern
W for West
a note sounding sharp is slightly too high

explanation.surface: A Japanese instrument from the East sounds out of tune compared with Western ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a container signal, but W cannot go inside SHARP; it just stands beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jew's harp is a small metal frame held in the mouth and twanged, a simple musical device.

clue.text: Theatre backer, not bold, abandoned play

indicators.note: not having something means it is taken out
abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose into new order

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the printer's abbreviation for bold

explanation.surface: A timid investor in a theatre walked away from a production.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre setting makes 'backer' look like the definition; it is just letters, and the play is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caretaker is Harold Pinter's 1960 drama about a tramp and two brothers, a famous stage work.

clue.text: Enemies in European and Irish rising

indicators.note: in a down entry rising goes from bottom to top, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: a Slav is a European from the east
Ir is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: Foes among Europeans and the Irish stage an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' suggests a revolt, as in the Easter Rising, but it turns the letters upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivals are opponents competing for the same goal, so they are foes in a looser sense.

clue.text: A bird going after bee, endlessly (and fly)

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off
going after means following, so those pieces are placed later

blocks.note: the word without its last letter
taken as written
the tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A bird chases a bee, and a fly too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like another insect in the chase, but it is the verb meaning to flee.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is slang for go away quickly, and to fly can mean to run off in haste.

clue.text: Shuns cat (hedgehog's partly free from injury)

indicators.note: partly means only a portion, so a run of letters is lifted from the words

blocks.note: the run starting after the first two letters

explanation.surface: A hedgehog avoids the cat and so escapes unhurt.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across three words: shUNS CAT HEDgehog, and the surface even acts out the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Unscathed means emerging without harm or a scratch, which is to be uninjured.

clue.text: Conscious of feature missing in tea set

indicators.note: whatever is missing in a group is absent from it, so letters are taken away

blocks.note: teaware is the crockery for serving tea
E.T. is the 1982 Spielberg feature film

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a piece is missing from the tea service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' suggests a characteristic, but it means a feature film, here E.T., whose two letters are scattered through TEAWARE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aware is to have knowledge or perception of something, a synonym for being awake to it.

clue.text: Horned beast losing oxygen and energy in river

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away

blocks.note: the rhino has a horn on its snout
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A rhinoceros struggles for breath and strength while wading in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The O of RHINO comes off and E takes its place at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is a major European waterway flowing from the Swiss Alps to the North Sea.

clue.text: Tax part of ... most of ... unsophisticated neckwear

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter
becoming part of something means being taken inside it

blocks.note: crass, missing its final letter
VAT, value added tax, is the British sales tax

explanation.surface: Taxing showy ties as part of a tirade against vulgar fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'part of' as a fraction of the tax; it means the tax goes inside the shortened adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Cravats are broad scarves or ties worn knotted around the throat, so they are items worn at the collar.

clue.text: Pop act of the '80s, The Firm?

blocks.note: first meaning: a 1980s new-wave singer with Antmusic hits, his stage name run together as one word
second meaning: unshakeable in resolve

explanation.walkthrough: 'The Firm' sounds like the name of a band or record label; it is simply the adjective, and the singer's name is run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adamant refuses to be swayed, so they are resolute and unyielding in a position.

clue.text: Where you see Italians get some shut-eye ... and the French

blocks.note: a nap is a short sleep
les is French for the, plural

explanation.surface: Italians, and the French too, enjoy an afternoon siesta.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'See Naples and die'.
explanation.definitionFit: Naples is a large southern Italian city, a place full of local people, so somewhere visitors meet them.

clue.text: Given three seconds, revolutionary lefty oddly missing kings, queens, etc

indicators.note: given here means added on, so pieces are joined together
with the odd letters missing only the even-numbered ones remain

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary
S is the abbreviation for second, three times
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A left-wing radical, given a few seconds, ends up without royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kings, queens' points to royalty, but these are the pieces on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess set contains the pieces of the board game: two kings and queens, plus bishops, knights, rooks and pawns.
